title: Suspension of a Disability Compensation Award
content:
**Causes of suspension.** A Disability Compensation award is suspended:

1. when the suspension count or more of payments come back within the rolling window of months — counted as the returned payments on the award whose funds were received back within that many calendar months ending on the current date;
2. when mail is returned and the veteran's whereabouts are unknown; or
3. when the veteran failed to report for a scheduled examination and the due-process period has run.

While suspended, the award releases no monthly payments.

**Retired clause on resumption.** The clause under which a suspended award resumed only after the veteran confirmed a current mailing address or payment account on this contact or reported for the examination is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Retired clause on the release of withheld months.** The clause under which, on resumption, the entitlement months withheld while the award was suspended — counted as the entitlement months with no monthly payment while the award status was suspended, from the first month withheld through the month before the resumption date — were released as one retroactive payment at the rates in effect for those months, less any debt offset, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Illustration of cause 1 (hypothetical, with the suspension count of 2 and the window of 12 months).** Two payments received back by VA in February and July of the same year, with the current date in October, are 2 returns within 12 months, and the award is suspended. One return within the window does not by itself suspend it.

superseded_clauses: A suspended award resumes only after the veteran confirms a current mailing address or payment account on this contact or reports for the examination.

On resumption, entitlement months withheld while the award was suspended (comp_msr_unpaid_running_months) are released as one retroactive payment at the rates in effect for those months, less any debt offset.
